required_manual_checks.description: The contract restores a trustworthy rollback build and nothing else: no product code, no migration, no schema/grant/data change, no script or smoke change, and nothing new goes live. It rebuilds exactly the commit the serving build came from, established with evidence: BUILD_ID k5DWIdCrqMPfXkxCGDdpW was built from ad86aa2 in 2A.3a-2 T9 (SLICE-2A3A2-CHECKPOINT.md). It records honestly what ROLLOUT-2A3BC-2's read-only preconditions found on 2026-09-30: the serving .next holds 867 iCloud-style duplicates (520 server/app, 286 server/chunks, 29 static/chunks, 12 build/chunks, 10 server/edge, 5 Turbopack cache, 2 static/media, 1 server/pages), none newer than BUILD_ID (862 dated 2026-09-21, 5 August); and the serving checkout sits on branch work/coordfreezedb001 at 1e7a5d5, not detached at ad86aa2 (the source difference is proof tooling and recovery-registry files only, which the running app does not load). The window switches the checkout to ad86aa2 detached before building.

Preconditions and steps with a pass condition and a failure row for each, modeled on ROLLOUT-2A3BC-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md. At minimum: Coordinator verify; only com.ascend.os on 3001 and no other session in the main checkout; a before-smoke on the current build using the PROMOTED smoke (`--baseline --release 2a3bc`, run from a detached worktree at the pin with .env.production.local linked for the run and removed after, the 2A.3a-2 T2 precedent), expected 0 failed with the 10 2a3bc checks failing as expected; record the contaminated .next's BUILD_ID, file count and duplicate count; bootout (not stop: KeepAlive); MOVE the contaminated .next aside to ~/AscendDeploy/<TS>/next-contaminated (never deleted by the agent; its deletion is a later owner decision); switch the serving checkout to ad86aa2 detached, clean; `npx next build --turbopack`; the duplicate check returns zero and gates the start; bootstrap after the build completes (build/restart race); /login 200; the same after-smoke with the same result; the counts in the two smoke records agree apart from ordinary use. Owner-run throughout.

Evidence that the rebuilt current version is clean, preserved in ~/AscendDeploy/<TS>/ (mode 0700, non-secret): the new BUILD_ID, the commit and tree it was built from, file count, a duplicate count of zero, and a manifest of the clean .next (every file path with its SHA-256, sorted) written outside iCloud immediately after the build and before the start. The manifest is what lets the rollout's T2 prove that its clone is byte-for-byte this clean build.

Failure rows for the cleanup itself. A failed build or a failed after-smoke restores the moved-aside .next (it served correctly; its contamination is unreferenced copies) and restarts the service, then reports: production is never left down to finish the cleanup. The rollout does not resume after a failed cleanup.

Amend ROLLOUT-2A3BC-EXECUTION-CONTRACT.md so it uses the cleaned build, without weakening it: the serving build is the BUILD_ID recorded by the cleanup (no longer k5DWIdCrqMPfXkxCGDdpW); P4 is re-run immediately before T0; T2's clone must match the cleanup manifest exactly (same paths, same SHA-256), with zero duplicates, and anything else is a STOP; the rollout window follows the cleanup in the same sitting where practical, under its own separate authorization, to keep the time for iCloud to re-contaminate the tree short; and §0's undeployed-range list admits this task's two documents, so the new pin passes the contract's own STOP rule. D5 stays postpone-only.

State and justify where the cleanup's execution evidence is recorded: in ROLLOUT-2A3BC-2's checkpoint (a 'Cleanup window' section) and ~/AscendDeploy, not in a separately promoted task. Every promotion before the rollout moves the deploy pin (D1: latest promoted baseline with P2 green) and forces a new full aggregate including owner R1b/R1c; this task's promoted commit becomes the pin, and the cleanup execution must not move it again.

Without production: build ad86aa2 in a clean worktree outside iCloud with `npx next build --turbopack` and record exit status, file count and duplicate count (expected zero), and exercise the exact manifest and comparison commands the contract uses, including a planted duplicate and a planted changed byte that the T2 comparison must reject. Record the results in the contract's evidence section.

The cleanup window needs its own owner authorization in chat (window start, and that the contract is the promoted one); the rollout window needs its separate authorization afterwards. Task creation, claim and promotion authorize nothing. Every production-touching or credential-bearing command is run by Oscar in his own terminal; the agent never types confirmations, reads .env.production.local values or runs admin commands.
The builder makes no production contact while building this task.

title: Restore a trustworthy rollback build: contract for a stopped-service rebuild of the serving commit (ad86aa2) with zero iCloud duplicates, and the ROLLOUT-2A3BC contract amended to use it (no production contact)
